statement: Let a permutation of [1, n] be a bijection p : {1, 2, ..., n} -> {1, 2, ..., n}, represented as a 1-indexed sequence of length n containing each integer from 1 to n exactly once. Call such a permutation self-divisible if for every i with 1 <= i <= n, gcd(p(i), i) = 1. Let C(n) be the number of self-divisible permutations of [1, n]. Whenever self_divisible_permutation_count(n) returns a result r, it holds that r = C(n).
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 12.

statement: self_divisible_permutation_count(n) returns a result (it does not fail, overflow, or panic).
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 12.

statement: Whenever self_divisible_permutation_count(n) returns a result r, 0 <= r <= n!, where n! = 1 * 2 * ... * n (and 0! = 1).
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 12.

statement: Whenever self_divisible_permutation_count(n) returns a result r, r <= odd_count(n) * (n-1)!, where odd_count(n) is the number of odd integers in {1, 2, ..., n}.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 12.

statement: Whenever self_divisible_permutation_count(n) returns a result r, r >= 1.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 12.

statement: Whenever self_divisible_permutation_count(n) returns a result r, r equals the permanent of the n x n matrix A (1-indexed) defined by A[i][j] = 1 if gcd(i, j) = 1, and A[i][j] = 0 otherwise. The permanent is sum_{p} product_{i=1}^n A[i][p(i)], where the sum is over all permutations p of {1, 2, ..., n}.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 12.
